title: Practice: Automating Spreadsheet Operations
prompt: Complete the hands-on worksheet task in the lesson for automating spreadsheet operations. Then enter the exact example expression or workflow text shown in the lesson code block below; this checks that you can recognize the demonstrated pattern, not whether you uploaded or executed an Excel workbook. Workbook quality and calculations still require the stated acceptance checks/human review.
objective: Apply Automating Spreadsheet Operations in a small, testable workbook task and compare the result with an expected output.
expected_output: Sets cell A1 on the active worksheet to Report ready. This is an illustrative Office Script; availability and tenant policy must be checked.

public_tests.name: Recognize the lesson example
public_tests.note: String check only; the example is visible in the lesson and does not execute a spreadsheet or verify a workbook artifact.

public_tests.name: Human-review acceptance
checklist: Workbook demonstrates the requested behavior with a small dataset.
Expected and actual output are compared.
One edge/failure case is checked and explained.

acceptance_criteria: The worksheet or workflow demonstrates the concept with correctly labeled inputs and stated assumptions.
The exact example expression/text can be identified and submitted for the server-side check.
Actual workbook output is independently verified; automated text grading is not treated as proof of workbook correctness.
hints: Start from a small known dataset and use the same sheet/column names as the example, or adapt the example and then submit the lesson expression exactly.
Check ranges, data types, locale and version compatibility before concluding the result is wrong.
Use the human-review checklist for any workbook artifact; the current exercise API does not ingest or inspect Excel files.
grading_method: Server checks exact text against the authored example only. It does not run Excel, read workbook files, prove calculations, or verify accessibility. Full artifact acceptance requires human review of the workbook and its test evidence.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed. Incorrect text receives no completion reward. The platform owns fixed, idempotent XP; no course-authored reward override is used.
